oil.summary: A sharp divergence dominated crude today: WTI tumbled 4.65% to $97.07 while Brent held flat near $108.78, leaving the WTI-Brent spread at an unusually wide $11.71. The gap reflects competing forces—Houthi strikes on Saudi airports and Aramco facilities earlier this week have kept Brent bid, while Trump's Russia sanctions waiver and the imminent arrival of the first Russian diesel tanker to the US are weighing on domestic benchmarks. Goldman Sachs flagged a new oil price shock risk, citing tanker rates surging from $3 to $20/bbl on Hormuz crisis disruption. Heating oil shed a punishing 7.09% as the Russia diesel deal undercuts distillate premiums. EIA data showed US crude inventories fell 3.1 million barrels last week, offering some floor, but Saudi Arabia's record-low production offset by a five-month high in exports adds further complexity to the supply picture. Markets are pricing an aggressive 77% probability of an OPEC cut at the next meeting.
drivers: Houthi strikes on Saudi Aramco facilities and airports supporting Brent; Trump's Russia sanctions waiver and incoming Russian diesel tanker pressuring WTI and heating oil
Goldman Sachs warns of oil price shock as tanker freight rates surge to $20/bbl from $3/bbl due to Iran war and Hormuz crisis
EIA reports US crude inventories -3.1 mb last week; Saudi exports hit five-month high despite record-low production; IOC to trim Middle East term purchases

gas.summary: Henry Hub natural gas slid 5.91% to $2.789/MMBtu, extending a brutal week that has seen US prices drop nearly 13%. TTF, by contrast, gained 2.87% to €87.5/MWh and is up over 19% on the month, underscoring the ongoing transatlantic supply bifurcation. The EU formally rejected reported US pressure to restore Russian gas flows as part of a Ukraine peace framework, keeping European supply anxiety elevated. The UK, responding to that tightness, approved the long-contested Jackdaw North Sea gas field—its first new North Sea project sanction since the Iran war pushed energy prices higher. On the demand side, GM's announcement that it will expand hybrid vehicle offerings as US pump prices hit $4.28/gal signals demand-side adaptation beginning to take hold.
drivers: Henry Hub drops sharply amid US supply-demand slack; TTF surges month-on-month as European supply tightness persists following Iran war disruptions
EU rejects US push to restore Russian gas imports under any Ukraine peace deal, keeping European supply risk premium intact
UK approves Jackdaw North Sea gas field in first new project sanction since the Iran war energy price shock

power.summary: The power and carbon complex offered thin data flow today. EU carbon EUAs were essentially unchanged at $81.495/EUA (+0.03%), with a modest week-on-month drift lower of about 1.2%, suggesting near-term carbon demand expectations remain subdued despite the broader energy price surge. TTF's 2.87% daily rise keeps gas-fired generation costs elevated across Europe. India's coal crisis is a notable macro risk: half the country's coal-fired fleet is reportedly operating with critically low stocks as power demand surges—a situation that could tighten seaborne thermal coal markets and indirectly pressure carbon prices if substitution shifts. Morgan Stanley flags global fuel markets remaining tight through at least mid-2027 due to elevated maintenance schedules, which could sustain power price volatility well into next year.
drivers: EU EUAs effectively flat at $81.50; TTF's continued monthly surge (+19%) raises gas-to-power generation costs across Europe
India coal crisis: half of coal power fleet at critically low stock levels amid surging power demand, raising seaborne coal market tightness risk
Morgan Stanley sees global fuel markets staying tight through mid-2027 on unusually high planned maintenance, sustaining power price volatility outlook
